subject: home-science
title: Adolescence: Charms and Challenges
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Adolescents think they are unique and nothing wrong can happen to them. Which cognitive characteristic does this demonstrate?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Adolescents who come under the influence of positive peer pressure are more likely to indulge in —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Abstract thinking during adolescence means adolescents —
options: have a strong sense of right and wrong
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Sunny is shouting at his mother as she is not allowing him to stay out late with his friends. If you were Sunny you would have —
options: not agreed to come in time
asked politely and agreed to come early
questions.answer: D

questions.q: Adolescents think everyone is watching them. This is called —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Menarche means —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Nocturnal emission is —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Adolescence is the age between —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: About how much of the adult height is gained during adolescence?
questions.answer: C

questions.q: Which of the following is specific to girls during adolescence?
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Self concept is said to be high when you look at your —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Which of these helps to decrease negative emotions?
options: Responding to situations in a healthy and positive way
questions.answer: A

options: Idolising stars and unhealthy body image
questions.answer: B

options: washing with clean water after urination
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Parents can help reduce the negative effects of media on their children. (ii) Social norms are a set of rules and expectations by which society guides the behaviour of its members. (iii) Adolescents look to their parents for approval and even change their behaviour to win their approval. (iv) Girls should remain indoors during menstruation.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – they look to their peers for approval. (iv) False – they should continue daily activities.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Everybody should wear cotton undergarments. (ii) Negative emotions can be decreased by responding to situations in a healthy and positive way. (iii) Adolescents should not trust anyone. (iv) Self concept can be high if you look at your strengths.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Boys should dry their undergarments in shade. (ii) Life skills help to improve the quality of life. (iii) Elderly people should let go of all responsibilities. (iv) Breast milk is the healthiest food for an infant.
questions.answer: (i) False – undergarments should be dried in the sun. (ii) True. (iii) False – they should slow down but may continue what they can. (iv) True.
questions.note: April 2025 had these four statements as Q31.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Adolescents are influenced by social norms and culture of the world. (ii) One should not feel guilty when refusing to smoke and drink. (iii) Parents should not discuss consequences of risk-taking behaviour with their children. (iv) Adolescents can learn job-related skills by on-the-job training.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – they should discuss them. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Empowering adolescents with critical thinking skills can reduce the negative impact of media. (ii) Actors and models influence youth's idea of a perfect body shape. (iii) Obsessive weight training is good for health. (iv) Adolescents should maintain dignity in their relationships.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) False – it is harmful. (iv) True.

questions.q: Match the characteristic with the example: (i) Abstract thinking (ii) Personal fable (iii) Imaginary audience (iv) Idealism; (a) believing everyone can see a tiny hole in the shirt (b) nothing bad can happen to me (c) understanding idioms and humour (d) strong sense of right and wrong.

State True or False: (i) A girl cannot become pregnant before her first period. (ii) Girls who bleed heavily need iron-rich food. (iii) Genital hygiene is important for both boys and girls. (iv) Children should not be told about adolescent changes.
questions.answer: (i) False – she can, as an egg is released before the first period. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – they should be prepared beforehand.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Puberty means the beginning of ______ maturity. (ii) Menstruation usually begins between ______ and 16 years. (iii) Sanitary napkins should be changed every ______ hours. (iv) A positive self concept leads to higher ______.
questions.answer: (i) sexual. (ii) 9. (iii) six. (iv) self-esteem.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Teenagers' ideal body shape is influenced by actors and models. What are the four negative effects of this on their health?
questions.answer: Eating disorders from excessive dieting; loss of stamina and decreased resistance to disease; irregular menstrual cycles in girls; obsessive weight training and use of steroids and supplements in boys with harmful effects.

questions.q: Your friend has stopped eating regular meals as she wants to look slim like film stars. Give four suggestions to help her.
questions.answer: Tell her that actors and models are not a realistic ideal; explain that crash dieting causes weakness, loss of stamina, poor resistance and irregular periods; encourage a balanced diet and exercise; build her self-esteem by accepting her body; limit exposure to such media and seek a doctor's or counsellor's advice.

questions.q: How are teenagers impacted by media and fashion? Give four examples.
questions.answer: They copy popular language, clothes, music and dance; they idolise stars and may lose their individuality; their idea of a perfect body shape changes, leading to dieting and eating disorders; exposure to violence and sexual images affects them negatively; media can also motivate them to take up sports and social work.

questions.q: Give two suggestions each to help Neha improve her relationship with her mother (two for Neha, two for the mother).
questions.answer: Neha: talk openly and respect her mother's point of view; help in household chores and talk courteously. Mother: involve Neha in family discussions and trust her; talk openly, understand and counsel her.

questions.q: What is meant by self concept and self-esteem?
questions.answer: Self concept is the way you see your strengths and weaknesses; self-esteem is your personal judgment of your abilities. A positive self concept leads to higher self-esteem.

questions.q: Explain 'peer' and give two positive effects of positive peer pressure.
questions.answer: A peer is a person of equal age, abilities, qualifications, background or social status. Positive peer pressure helps social development and self-esteem, gives a safety net in difficult times, provides role models and encourages healthy behaviour such as sports.

questions.q: Write any four tips for maintaining genital hygiene in adolescence.
questions.answer: Wash with clean water after urination; use cotton undergarments; change undergarments daily and dry them in the sun; change stained garments at once; keep pubic hair trimmed; use clean sanitary napkins changed every six hours.

questions.q: Mention four ways to say 'no' assertively to peer pressure.
questions.answer: Use the word 'no' rather than 'I can't'; do not feel guilty or say sorry; keep eye contact and consistent body language; change the topic, ignore the question and walk off, or assertively convince; do not give reasons for every action.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Make the girls aware of any three myths and facts regarding menstruation.
questions.answer: Myth: girls should not work during menstruation – Fact: they should continue daily activities; walking and exercise relieve cramps. Myth: bathing causes cramps – Fact: a warm bath soothes muscles; bathe daily. Myth: women should not enter the kitchen or handle pickle – Fact: there is no scientific evidence for such restrictions. Myth: it is alright to take medicine to delay periods – Fact: avoid it without a doctor's advice.

questions.q: Describe the cognitive characteristics of adolescents with an example of each (any three).
questions.answer: Abstract thinking – they can imagine the impossible and understand idioms and humour. Personal fable – they think they are unique and nothing bad can happen, so they take risks. Systematic thinking – they can list alternatives and their consequences, e.g. planning a holiday. Idealism – a strong sense of right and wrong. Imaginary audience – they think everyone is watching them, e.g. a small hole in the T-shirt.

questions.q: Explain how parents can reduce the negative effect of media on adolescents.
questions.answer: Help them distinguish fantasy from reality; discuss the consequences of violence and risk-taking behaviour; empower them with critical thinking and decision-making skills so they filter messages and watch age-appropriate content.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Give five suggestions to adolescents to deal with negative peer pressure.
questions.answer: (1) Do not give in because everyone else is doing it. (2) Say 'no' firmly rather than 'I can't', without guilt. (3) Keep body language and eye contact consistent with the words. (4) Use techniques such as changing the topic or walking away. (5) Do not give reasons for every action and maintain your dignity. (6) Choose friends who encourage healthy behaviour and share problems with parents or trusted persons. (7) Practise assertive skills before the situation arises.

questions.q: Write any five physical changes in adolescent girls.
questions.answer: Increase in height and weight; growth of breasts; broadening of hips; growth of underarm and pubic hair; pimples or acne; development of reproductive organs; menarche (start of menstruation).

or.q: Suggest any five ways to develop self-esteem in adolescents.
or.answer: Accept strong points and appreciate them; acknowledge weaknesses and work on them; accept physical aspects that cannot be changed; avoid self-pity; seek advice from a trusted friend, parent or counsellor; appreciate others honestly; eat healthy and exercise; take pride in abilities and success.
